The garments are designed to interfere with artificial intelligence systems that use computer vision to detect people. At first glance, the clothing appears to feature an abstract graphic pattern, but the textile design is specifically developed to disrupt object-recognition algorithms used in surveillance, security, and autonomous systems. The pattern is based on the concept of an adversarial attack, in which visual data is manipulated so that a machine incorrectly interprets what it sees. When worn, the garments are intended to make the wearer difficult for AI-based person detectors to recognize, disrupting the system’s ability to identify the human figure. all images courtesy of Simon Weckert Continuous Adversarial Texture Covers Garment Surface Previous attempts to evade AI person-detection systems have relied on fixed printed patches, which can become ineffective when fabric folds or camera angles change. This vulnerability is known as the segment-missing problem. Digital Camouflage by designer Simon Weckert addresses this issue through a seamless Adversarial Texture (AdvTexture) that covers the entire garment. The continuous pattern is generated using a specialized generative AI method known as TC-EGA, which optimizes a tileable textile design. Applied across the full surface of the garment, the texture produces high-frequency visual noise and false visual features from different viewing angles, disrupting the consistency required for AI-based object recognition. The collection is manufactured in Latvia using a durable blend of 65% recycled polyester and 35% polyester. The adversarial texture is applied through digital textile printing, combining computational pattern generation with textile production to create garments designed to challenge machine-based systems of visual recognition. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/08/ethi.text: Ethiopian drone strikes have targeted Eritrean forces who had reached a northern Tigrayan city, a conflict monitor and witnesses said on Thursday, amid fears that the renewed fighting in the African country might turn into a wider regional war.The strikes came as the Tigray People's Liberation Front-led seven-group rebel coalition continued to push against federal forces across northern Ethiopia, with fighting reported in Afar and Amhara regions since the coalition announced its offensive last week.Eritrean troops crossed the border this week and were positioned around the Ethiopian city of Adigrat in northern Tigray, according to multiple sources.Conflict monitor ACLED said "Eritrean troops and ammunition" in the Adigrat area were hit by "multiple drone strikes" overnight between Wednesday and Thursday."There were many, many drone strikes yesterday. Some Eritrean lorries have been destroyed. They are no longer in the streets," one witness, who spoke on condition of anonymity, told AFP.Another witness in Adigrat, who also asked for anonymity, said they had heard a "massive explosion during the night"."I also saw Eritrean military vehicles that had been hit by a drone," they added.A third witness said Eritrean troops appeared to be retreating north.Relations between the two neighbouring countries, which fought a border war from 1998 to 2000, have deteriorated again in recent months.Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing rebels in its northern Tigray state, and the two countries severed diplomatic ties last week.The government in Asmara in turn accuses Ethiopia of supporting its own opponents, and of looking for a pretext to invade its territory and seize direct access to the Red Sea.Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Meskel said on X that Ethiopia was "openly working to bring about regime change in Eritrea by providing shelter and support to certain mercenaries who claim to be opposition".Neither Ethiopia nor Eritrea has responded to questions about the fighting.Alliance turned uglyEritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, cutting off the latter from access to the Red Sea.After years of war and tension, relations improved markedly after Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed rose to power in 2018, an effort he was rewarded for with a Nobel Peace Prize.Eritrea even fought alongside Ethiopia during the latter's 2020-2022 civil war against the TPLF.But the relationship deteriorated soon after, with Eritrea voicing anger over the terms of the peace agreement that ended that war and, later on, Ethiopia's claims that it has a right to sea access.Abiy's rhetoric escalated to claim that allowing Eritrea's independence was a "mistake," as Ethiopia accused Eritrean troops of crimes against civilians during the 2020-2022 Tigray war.This and other accusations prompted Eritrea to blast Ethiopia for allegedly "floating false flags to justify the war that it has been itching to unleash for two long years".Sparks flew again in February, when Addis Ababa accused its neighbour of sending troops across the border, an allegation Asmara slammed as "false".Addis Ababa has further pointed a finger at Eritrea, but also at Sudan and Egypt for allegedly supporting the TPLF-led alliance in the latest escalation of fighting.Last Thursday, Ethiopia expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats and shut its embassy in Asmara, while Eritrea responded that it would "sever all diplomatic ties".

https://bnn-news.com/politics/latvia-s-s.text: Leader of the United List (AS) alliance and Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs. · Photo: Paula Čurkste/LETA Advertisements With around 99% of the votes counted in Latvia’s 15th Saeima election, the United List (AS) has secured a decisive victory, winning 42 seats in parliament. The number of seats won by AS is the best result achieved by any political force in a Saeima election since the restoration of Latvia’s independence. By comparison, Latvian Way won 36 seats in 1993, Unity secured 33 seats in 2010, while Harmony won 31 seats in the 2011 snap election. Meanwhile, voter turnout in the 15th Saeima election was the lowest since the restoration of independence – only 51.8% of eligible voters participated this year. Votes still need to be counted by just 30 postal voting commissions, while the counting of positive and negative candidate marks still needs to be completed at a larger number of polling stations. Advertisements Preliminary election results show that only six parties will enter the next Saeima, while the Union of Greens and Farmers (ZZS) is the first political force to fall short of the 5% electoral threshold. With the vote count effectively complete, AS has received 35.3% of the vote. Latvia First (LPV) is in second place with 13.1%, followed by the Sovereign Power/Young Latvians alliance (SV/AJ) with 11.74%. The National Alliance (NA) received 8.91% of the vote, the Progressives 7.81%, and New Unity (JV) 6.34%. Accordingly, AS will hold 42 seats in the Saeima, LPV 17, SV/AJ 15, NA 10, the Progressives nine and JV seven. Advertisements The remaining eight parties that contested the election have fallen below the 5% threshold. ZZS received 4.41% of the vote, We Are Changing the Rules 3.43%, and Latvia’s Development 2.18%. These parties will be eligible for state funding because they received more than 2% of the vote. Just below the 2% threshold is Stability! with 1.99% support, followed by Rising Sun for Latvia (ASL) with 1.33%, Gobzems’ List with 0.98%, Harmony Centre with 0.82%, and the New Conservative Party with 0.33%. All of these parties, with the exception of ASL, had previously received state funding.
